'''Kevin Séraphin''' (born 7 December 1989) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m|2}} tall, Séraphin played at both the [[power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kevin_seraphin/|title=Kevin Séraphin Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 23, 2013}}</ref> in his playing career. Séraphin started his professional basketball career in [[Cholet Basket]], and was drafted 17th overall in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]], but was later traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].

==Professional career==
===Cholet Basket (2007–2010)===
In December 2007, Séraphin joined the [[Cholet Basket]] senior team for the first time after having played for their junior team since 2006. In August 2009, he signed a three-year contract extension with Cholet.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/eurocup/78551/cholet-first-pro-contract-for-seraphin.html Cholet, first pro contract for Seraphin]</ref> In the 2009–10 season, he played 32 games, averaging 6.0 points and 4.2 rebounds per game as he went on to help Cholet win the [[2009–10 Pro A season|2009–10 Pro A]] championship. He also earned the 2010 Most Improved Player award.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/81382/traore-and-greer-mvps-of-pro-a.html Traoré and Greer MVPs of Pro A]</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2010–2015)===
[[File:Kevin Seraphin Lou Amundson.jpg|thumb|203x203px|Séraphin against [[Lou Amundson]]]]
[[File:Kevin Seraphin Wizards.jpg|thumb|Kevin Seraphin grabbing a rebound]]
On 24 June 2010 Séraphin was selected with the 17th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. On 8 July 2010 he was traded, along with [[Kirk Hinrich]] and cash considerations, to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for the rights to [[Vladimir Veremeenko]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Wizards Acquire Kirk Hinrich and Draft Rights to Kevin Seraphin From Chicago | url = http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/hinrich-seraphin_100708.html | date=July 8, 2010 | access-date = July 8, 2010 | work = NBA.com}}</ref> On 30 July 2010 he signed his rookie scale contract with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web | title = Wizards sign Seraphin to rookie deal | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5424592 | date=July 30, 2010 | access-date = July 30, 2010 | work = ESPN.com}}</ref>

On 20 September 2011 Séraphin signed with [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]] of Spain for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/87464/5611/caja-laboral-adds-seraphin-to-frontline |title=CAJA LABORAL adds Seraphin to frontline |work=Euroleague.net |date=September 20, 2011 |access-date=September 20, 2011}}</ref> In December 2011, he returned to the Wizards following the conclusion of the lockout.

On 30 June 2014 the Wizards tendered a $3.89 million qualifying offer to make Séraphin a restricted free agent. On 18 July 2014 he accepted the one-year, $3.89 million qualifying offer.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/wizards-re-sign-kevin-seraphin--garrett-temple-231417544.html Wizards re-sign Kevin Seraphin, Garrett Temple]</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Seraphin signs qualifying offer |date=2014-07-19 |website=[[The Washington Post]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211081052/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/seraphin-signs-qualifying-offer/2014/07/18/151a98b4-0eda-11e4-b0dd-edc009ac1f9d_story.html |archive-date=2019-12-11 |url-status=live |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/seraphin-signs-qualifying-offer/2014/07/18/151a98b4-0eda-11e4-b0dd-edc009ac1f9d_story.html}}</ref><ref>[http://www.csnwashington.com/basketball-washington-wizards/talk/kevin-seraphin-signs-38-million-qualifying-offer-wizards Kevin Seraphin signs $3.8 million qualifying offer with Wizards]</ref>

===New York Knicks (2015–2016)===
On 6 August 2015 Séraphin signed with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-kevin-seraphin|title=Knicks Sign Kevin Seraphin|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2015|access-date=August 6, 2015}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2016–2017)===
On 8 September 2016 Séraphin signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-kevin-seraphin-and-nick-zeisloft|title=Pacers Sign Kevin Seraphin and Nick Zeisloft|work=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> On 31 July 2017 he was waived by the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kevin-seraphin-waived-by-pacers/|title=Kevin Seraphin: Waived by Pacers|work=cbssports.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=July 31, 2017}}</ref>

===Barcelona (2017–2019)===
On 4 August 2017 Séraphin signed a two-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona Lassa]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona strengthens frontline with Seraphin|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/83n7hpijmi4kivxe|access-date=August 4, 2017|work=euroleague.net|date=August 4, 2017}}</ref> On 17 February 2019 he won [[2019 Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|2019 Copa del Rey]], recording six points and one rebound in a 94–93 win over [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].

On 24 October 2020 Séraphin announced he was retiring from professional basketball, citing a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Kevin Seraphin announces decision to retire |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1118914/kevin-seraphin-announces-decision-to-retire/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=October 24, 2020 |date=October 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Seven-year NBA veteran Kevin Seraphin retires from basketball at age 30 |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/10/24/seven-year-nba-veteran-kevin-seraphin-retires-from-basketball-at-age-30/ |website=nba.nbcsports.com |access-date=October 26, 2020 |date=October 24, 2020}}</ref>

==National team career==
Séraphin was named to the All-Tournament team of the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], after helping France to win the silver medal. He was a member of the senior [[France national basketball team|French national basketball team]] in 2011, where France reached the finals of the [[EuroBasket 2011]], which they lost to [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]].<ref>[http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2011/Sep/18/spain-beats-france-to-win-european-championship/ Spain beats France to win European Championship]</ref> He played for France at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/se/kevin-seraphin-1.html|title=Kevin Seraphin Bio, Stats, and Results|website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417194159/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/se/kevin-seraphin-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2020-04-17|access-date=2018-12-03}}</ref>
